title: Opowiadanie · spójniki
note:
B1 Block 6 opener (vocab leaf) — the narrative connectives named on B1-SPINE.md's own line for this node: najpierw, potem, w końcu, nagle, niestety. All five confirmed genuinely new via check_new.py before writing a single string (spine flagged 'potem was confirmed untaught during A2' — reconfirmed here, still true). Added a sixth, na szczęście, as the natural opposite of niestety (fortunately/unfortunately) — a contrast pair is easier to anchor than niestety alone, and it keeps the set at a clean 6 rather than stretching the spine's list artificially; also confirmed NEW via check_new.py before adding. This is the unit the spine's own note calls out as the real B1 milestone: it unlocks TELLING A STORY by giving the sequencing words that string together everything already owned (past tense, aspect, motion, virile agreement) into a narrative.

ZERO NEW STRUCTURES — every sentence recycles a structure already live: past_byc, past_plural, aspect_past, motion_prefixed (b1_arrive_leave's przyjechał/przyszedł, not the generic aspect_past twins — checked the pack's own teaches_structures before tagging), sie_reflexive, prep_do_gen, prep_w_loc, negation, can_inf, and one virile_past example (oni byli) since that unit is already live on the path. Each sentence gives exactly one new item — the connective — anchored by fully recycled material, per the anchor rule.

DROPPED FROM THE DRAFT, logged: an early draft used 'było zimno' as a nagle example, assuming it was covered by the weather_chunk catalogue description ('fixed past 3sg chunks... było zimno' — SEQUENCING.md's own structure-catalogue row). check_new.py returned NEW — the catalogue row describes what weather_chunk is *for*, not what any live pack has actually tagged in teaches_lemmas yet; no live pack teaches było zimno as a string. Replaced with 'Nagle zgubiłem klucz.' (zgubiłem is a confirmed b1_journeys teach). Logged here so whoever next reaches for a weather-past chunk from that catalogue row checks it first rather than assuming the catalogue description is itself a teach record.

HOMOGRAPH CHECK: none of the six connectives collide with any earlier-taught string under a different sense — all six came back clean NEW, not reused spellings.

All recycled content (byłem/byłam, robiliśmy, kupiłem/chleb, byliśmy, przyjechał/pociąg, przyszedł/tata, zgubiłem/klucz, spóźniłam się/do pracy, nie mogę teraz rozmawiać, nie spóźniłem się, oni/byli) verified TAUGHT via check_new.py, each against its owning pack, before being used — no homograph risk found on any of them (e.g. klucz/tata/pociąg are the same senses their owning packs taught, not a different meaning of the same string).

items.explain: w końcu is built on koniec, the 'end' you already know, but it's a fixed idiom — it doesn't mean a literal place, it means eventually / finally, after some delay or difficulty.
na szczęście and niestety are opposites — the two words a story uses to say whether the surprise was good or bad. Worth learning as a pair.

sentences.explain: przyjechał is the arrive-by-vehicle verb from the last block — one finished arrival.

Unfortunately I can't talk right now.
